answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, externally issued credential or stake before it can vote on work or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital and risk losing it; splitting a fixed stake across accounts does not multiply voting weight. An atlas of claims may look impressive, while a sable-colored profile or a fable of unique expertise proves nothing without the costly bond.
